title: Deep Space - A Sci-Fi Space Game Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track science fiction game score: bridge, station, drift, the derelict, ship battles, bosses and cues. MIDI + OGG.
description:
Deep Space is a 44 track score for space games: the bridge and the engine room, a station and its cantina, drift and the nebula, planetfall and alien ruins, a derelict to board, ship battles, two bosses and the cues a game fires all day.

One move, every track. Every track on this record turns on a chromatic mediant: two major chords, one after the other, whose roots are a third apart, like D to F in the title theme. No key contains that pair, so the harmony steps outside the key for a moment, a move film and game scores have long used for scale and wonder. Checked bar by bar on the shipped MIDI: 62 such moves across all 44 tracks, at least one in every track. Run the same reading over the other 25 albums in this studio's catalogue, 993 tracks, and 18 of them carry one; no album carries one on every track.

Orchestra and synthesizer, one voice. Horns, trumpets, strings, choir and harp share the score with saw and square leads, synth basses and synth pads, so the bridge and the battle belong to the same ship. 31 General MIDI sounds in all, five modes (Ionian, Mixolydian, Lydian, Dorian and Aeolian) across 42 keys.

What is in it. 34 full pieces and 10 short cues, 45:28 of music. The ship: Beyond the Heliopause, The Bridge, Charting the Reach, Crew Quarters, The Engine Room, Hydroponics Deck, Cryosleep and Docking Clamps. The station: Meridian Station; Meridian, Night Cycle; The Last Light Cantina; and The Exchange. Out in the dark: Drift; Inside the Nebula; The Asteroid Belt; Over the Gas Giant; Planetfall; The Glass Plains; The Precursor Vault; The Derelict; Deck Nine, No Power; A Signal from Nowhere; and Event Horizon. Danger: All Hands to Stations, The Jump, Fighters Inbound, Broadside at Kestrel Gate, Corridor Firefight, Running Dark, The Dreadnought and The Voidmother. After: Debris and Starlight, For Those Lost in the Dark and The Long Way Home. Cues: Jump Complete, Hostile Contact, Docking Confirmed, Incoming Transmission, Salvage Recovered, Systems Upgraded, New Orders, Uncharted System, Sector Clear and Hull Breach.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 34 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

One family of 5 cells. Beacon, Orbit, Thrust, Horizon and Void. Beacon leaps a fifth and opens the title, the bridge and the way home; Orbit turns it over for the dark outside the hull; Thrust pulls it in to steps for work and travel; Horizon widens it for wonder; Void falls away, and every fight opens on it. 1464 statements and fragments of those cells across the album, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI.

Gate results. 780 theory checks and 498 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: Beyond the Heliopause, the title theme, The Jump, the hyperspace loop, and The Voidmother, the final boss.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, so the MIDI is yours to re voice with your own instruments. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.
